claim: An ECS service runs and maintains a specified number of instances of a task definition in a cluster; if a task fails or stops, the service scheduler launches another instance to replace it and so keeps the desired number of tasks.
question: What does the ECS service scheduler do when a task fails or stops?

values.display: run and maintain a specified number of instances of a task definition
launches another instance of your task definition to replace it

evidence.quote: You can use an Amazon ECS service to run and maintain a specified number of instances of a task definition simultaneously in an Amazon ECS cluster. If one of your tasks fails or stops, the Amazon ECS service scheduler launches another instance of your task definition to replace it. This helps maintain your desired number of tasks in the service.

claim: An ECS blue/green deployment runs two identical production environments, blue and green; it lets you validate new service revisions before directing production traffic to them, and the production environment remains available throughout the deployment.

values.display: running two identical production environments called blue and green
Zero downtime deployments

evidence.quote: A blue/green deployment is a release methodology that reduces downtime and risk by running two identical production environments called blue and green. With Amazon ECS blue/green deployments, you can validate new service revisions before directing production traffic to them.
Zero downtime deployments. The production environment remains available throughout the deployment process, ensuring continuous service availability.

claim: ECS blue/green deployments temporarily run both the blue and green service revisions simultaneously, which may double your resource usage during deployments, and the blue revision is kept running until the bake time expires so rollback is easier.

values.display: may double your resource usage during deployments
the blue revision is kept running until the bake time expires

evidence.quote: Resource usage: Blue/green deployments temporarily run both the blue and green service revisions simultaneously, which may double your resource usage during deployments.
Rollback: Blue/green deployments make it easier to roll back to the previous version if issues are detected, as the blue revision is kept running until the bake time expires.

claim: With Availability Zone rebalancing, Amazon ECS continuously monitors the distribution of tasks across Availability Zones and, when it detects an uneven distribution, automatically rebalances by launching new tasks in the zones with the fewest tasks and terminating tasks in the overloaded zones.
question: What does ECS Availability Zone rebalancing do?

values.display: continuously monitors the distribution of tasks across Availability Zones
launching new tasks in the Availability Zones with the fewest tasks

evidence.quote: With Availability Zone rebalancing, Amazon ECS continuously monitors the distribution of tasks across Availability Zones for each of your services. When Amazon ECS detects an uneven task distribution, it automatically takes action to rebalance the workload across Availability Zones. This involves launching new tasks in the Availability Zones with the fewest tasks and terminating tasks in the overloaded Availability Zones.

claim: Starting September 5, 2025, Amazon ECS enables Availability Zone rebalancing for all eligible services; a service is eligible when Availability Zone spread is the first task placement strategy or when there is no placement strategy.
